title: Installs through cs-npmrevs fail once the build store holds enough npm packages
foundBy: session agent, investigating campaign's failed `make repin` of 2026-09-29

evidence.verified: Against a stand-in server that exits at once, `with-npmrevs.sh` failed in 0.35 s and printed its log. Against one that took 24 s to listen, it waited and ran the command. Campaign's `make repin`, rerun with these scripts against the same unpruned store, moved the `@codesweep-ai/ui` pin and rebuilt the viewer in 31 s. `python3 -m unittest tests.test_record_build`: 18 of 18 pass, and test_a_recorded_build_removes_the_npm_packages_of_older_ones fails against the previous record-build.sh. `make check` passed. Run over a copy of the owner's store, the prune took npm/ from 179 packages (311 MB) to 47 (83 MB).

resolution: `scripts/with-npmrevs.sh` now waits as long as the registry runs, up to a minute, and stops at once if it exits. Each recorded build removes the npm packages of older ones. A project keeps them for its three newest builds recorded within three days, and for its newest whatever its age. Entries, modules and images stay, and a store that is a repository, as a campaign's is, is left whole.
details: `scripts/with-npmrevs.sh` starts cs-npmrevs and gave it 50 checks, about 10 seconds, to answer. cs-npmrevs reads every package it serves before it listens, and it serves the owner's build store, where nothing removed old npm packages. By 2026-09-29 the store held 179 packages (311 MB), startup took about 9 seconds, and campaign's `make repin` failed with `the registry did not come up`. Each clean `make ci` in lint, ledger or npmrevs adds five more packages, and `npm run ci` in ui adds one.
